full_judgment:
2. Respondent No.1 as the petitioner (hereinafter referred to as the writ-petitioner) filed the said writ petition before the High Court Division challenging the order dated 08.05.2006 passed by the Deputy Administrator of Waqfs-1, Bangladesh (writ-respondent No. 3) in Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 2005 (E.C. No. 14858, Dhaka) communicated vide his office Memo No. 3/226(5) in Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 2005 cancelling the lease of the writ-petition "to have been passed and made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect" and the Rule Nisi was issued accordingly. 

 3. In the writ petition, the writ-petitioner stated, inter alia, that on 01.01.1946, one Sheikh, son of late Sheikh Azim Baks created Waqf-E-Lillah in respect of 29 acre land for the maintenance of the local mosque with a provision that Waqif should be the first Mutawalli and while he had been managing the Waqf Estate, he died leaving behind two sons: Didar Baks and Shamsuddin. On 29.03.1965, Didar Baks enrolled the Waqf Estate in the office of respondent No. 2 (the Administrator of Waqfs) vide E.C. No. 14858 (Sheikh Hafizullah Waqf Estate), Dhaka as its Mutawalli. After the death of Didar Baks, another son of the Waqif named Shamsuddin stepped into the shoes of his deceased elder brother as third Mutawalli on 28.12.1987. Shamsuddin tendered resignation from the office of Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate. Then Md. Selim, respondent No.5, was appointed as the Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate by respondent No. 2 on 16.01.1993. In the meantime, during the tenure of the aforesaid successive Mutawallis, 50% of waqf property was illegally transferred to different persons; as a result "the wishes of the Waqif has been broken down" and the Waqf Estate feel into a stagnant position which compelled respondent No. 5 (Md. Selim) to file an application on 09.08.1998 (to whom the application was filed has not been stated, but presumably it would be the Administrator of Waqfs) for leasing out 5(five) kathas of waqf land (ditch in nature) to the writ-petitioner for 20(twenty) years and the writ-petitioner also filed an application for lease (again person to whom the application was filed has not been mentioned). The local Waqf Inspector made inquiry and submitted his report on 21.09.998 and the Assistant Administrator (Finance) of the office the Administrator of Waqfs also made inquiry and submitted his report in detailed with recommendation for leasing out the land of the Waqf Estate and on the basis of the applications as well as the inquiry reports, the Administrator of Waqfs, Bangladesh by his order dated 15.12.1998 granted lease vide his office Memo No. ০১২৬৩/ঢাঃদঃ with a condition of renewal of the lease after every five years. As per the aforesaid order for granting lease, a lease agreement was executed in between the Mutawalli and the writ-petitioner on 31.012.1998 for a period of 20 years with effect from 31.12.1998 fixing a rent of taka 3,500.00 per month with a stipulation for enhancement of the rate of the rent at the rate of taka 500.00 after every five years along with a further stipulation that if the lessee failed to pay the rent for three months, he should be treated as defaulter and in that case, the lease would stand cancelled. There was also a condition that the lessee would develop the ditch land at his own cost and establish his biscuit factory there-in. After taking lease for 20 years, the writ-petitioner spent taka 23,800,000.00 and established his biscuit factory in the leasehold land under the name and style "Chendhury Food Products" and used to run his business through salaried employees and labourers erecting huts in some portion of the leasehold land having trade licensee from Dhaka City Corporation. The writ-petitioner brought the fact of his expenditure to the notice of the Administrator of Waqfs, Bangladesh on 26.11.2000. The writ-petitioner, as per the condition of the lease deed as well as the lease granting order, regularly paid the rent along with the increased rate upto May, 2006. Respondent No. 5 being a heroine addicted almost used to suffer imprisonment in jail custody and in those circumstances, his wife Mrs. Zarina Begum used to look after the Waqf Estate and received rent. After the expiry of five years of the lease period, the writ-petitioner on 08.12.2003 filed an application to respondent No. 2, the Administrator of Waqfs for renewal of the period of lease. 

 7. Mr. Momtaz Uddin Fakir, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submits that, in fact, the lease of the waqf property in question was given to the writ-petitioner   for 5 (five) years only, but the High Court Division overlooking the terms of the order of the Administrator of Waqfs dated 15.12.1998 accepted the lease for a period of 20 (twenty) years and thus erred in law in making the Rule Nisi absolute. He further submits that the Administrator of Waqfs by giving an elaborate order cancelled the lease of the writ-petitioner on the clear finding that he violated the terms of the lease which were fundamentally the question of fact, but the High Court Division without considering the said aspect of the case made the. Rule Nisi absolute and as such, the impugned judgment and order cannot be sustained and the same calls for interference by this Court by giving leave. 

 The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is modified to the extent that the order of the Deputy Administrator of Waqfs canceling the lease order, refusing to renew the lease and direction upon the lessee (the writ-petitioner) to surrender vacant possession of the leasehold land is restored. The writ-petitioner-respondent is directed to vacate the leasehold property of the waqf in question and hand over possession thereof to the present Mutawalli within 1 (one) month from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment. In case, the writ-petitioner-respondent fails to vacate the leasehold property and deliver possession thereof to the Mutawalli the Administrator of Waqfs shall take necessary steps for his eviction therefrom. And if there is any due from the writ-petitioner-respondent, the Mutawalli shall take necessary steps for realization of the same in accordance with law.
